title: Protect the meter with a shunt
story: An old needle meter (modelled as the 1 kOhm resistor RM) reads full scale at 1 mA and is damaged above that. You want it to measure a 10 mA current instead. Put a shunt resistor in parallel with the meter so that, when 10 mA arrive, the meter gets between 0.85 mA and 1.0 mA and the rest bypasses it.

goals.label: meter current between 0.85 mA and 1.0 mA

hints: The meter's share is I x R_shunt / (R_meter + R_shunt). You want that share to be about one tenth of 10 mA.
The ideal shunt carries 9 mA while the meter carries 1 mA at the same voltage, so the shunt must be about 9 times smaller than 1 kOhm. Round to a value that keeps the meter safe.
